title: Meta Cuts 8,000 Jobs in 4 AM Email Blitz as Zuckerberg Admits Mistakes in AI Pivot
excerpt: The largest layoff round since Meta s 2022-2023 restructuring arrives alongside a 145 billion dollar AI spending plan, employee monitoring backlash, and a CEO acknowledging the company has stumbled in execution.
body:
• Meta laid off approximately 8,000 employees, roughly 10% of its global workforce, with notification emails sent at 4 AM local time starting in Singapore on May 20.
  • The company simultaneously reassigned 7,000 employees to AI-focused teams and canceled 6,000 open positions, reshaping nearly 20% of its workforce.
  • CEO Mark Zuckerberg acknowledged the human cost of the restructuring in an internal memo, admitting the company had "made mistakes" while pledging no further company-wide layoffs this year.
  • Meta's 2026 capital expenditure forecast of $125 billion to $145 billion, more than double its 2025 outlay, is funding the aggressive pivot to AI infrastructure and foundational models.

Meta Platforms has completed its largest workforce reduction since the 2022-2023 "Year of Efficiency," cutting approximately 8,000 jobs globally while funneling billions into AI infrastructure in a restructuring that underscores the human cost of Big Tech's artificial intelligence arms race.

The 4 AM Layoff Emails

Notification emails began landing in employee inboxes at 4 AM local time on May 20, starting with Meta's Asian hub in Singapore before rolling westward through Europe and the United States, according to Business Insider. Employees across impacted regions, including the U.S. and Britain, had been instructed to work from home ahead of the notifications.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-pnxefltaQ4

The cuts targeted engineering roles, integrity operations, cybersecurity, content design, and Reality Labs teams. U.S.-based employees are receiving severance packages that include 16 weeks of base pay, an additional two weeks for every year of service, and 18 months of healthcare coverage, according to an internal document.

"It's always sad to say goodbye to people who have contributed to our mission and to building this company. I feel the weight of that."

— Mark Zuckerberg, Meta CEO, in internal memo

AI Pivot at Scale

The layoffs are one piece of a sweeping organizational overhaul. Meta simultaneously canceled 6,000 open positions and reassigned more than 7,000 employees to AI-focused teams, meaning nearly one in five workers across the company is being repositioned, according to Reuters.

Chief People Officer Janelle Gale told employees in a memo that many teams can now operate with "a flatter structure with smaller teams of pods/cohorts," adding that the company believes this "will make us more productive and make the work more rewarding."

Chief Technology Officer Andrew Bosworth articulated the new operating philosophy bluntly: "Our agents primarily do the work. Our role is to direct, review and help them improve."

Meta's 2026 capital expenditure forecast stands at $125 billion to $145 billion, more than double its 2025 outlay of $72.2 billion. In a single quarter, the company added $107 billion in contractual commitments for cloud and infrastructure deals, according to Yahoo Finance. The money is flowing into data centers, AI chips, and the Meta Superintelligence Labs division that Zuckerberg launched last year.

Morale and the Cost of Restructuring

Internal sentiment has turned sharply negative. Employees have openly criticized Zuckerberg and other leaders on Meta's internal message forum, according to Reuters. More than 1,500 employees signed a petition opposing a workplace monitoring initiative that tracks mouse movements, clicks, and keystrokes to train AI models, with Meta executives declining requests to opt out.

Compensation decisions have compounded the frustration. Meta cut annual raises by 5% in February 2026 on top of a 10% trim the year before, according to Moneywise. Median total compensation at the company fell from $417,400 in 2024 to $388,200 in 2025, Wired reported. Meanwhile, Zuckerberg has been personally recruiting AI researchers with packages reportedly reaching $100 million.

"Everyone is unhappy; the only people who are not unhappy are, literally, executives."

— Anonymous Instagram employee, as reported by Wired

Zuckerberg's Acknowledgment

In a follow-up memo leaked to Reuters in June, Zuckerberg struck a more conciliatory tone. "Given the complexity of these changes, we've made mistakes and will almost certainly make more," he wrote, adding that he is "focused on providing as much stability as possible" going forward.

He pledged no further company-wide layoffs this year, though Chief People Officer Gale did not rule out targeted cuts in specific functions. Zuckerberg framed the restructuring as preparation rather than retreat, describing Meta as "one of the few companies positioned to help define the future" with a goal of delivering "personal superintelligence" to users worldwide.

What Comes Next

Meta ended Q1 with 77,900 employees, down 1% from the previous quarter, after posting $56.31 billion in revenue, a 33% jump from the prior year. The company's 2025 revenue hit $201 billion, up 22% year-over-year. By the financial metrics, Meta is not a company in distress. It is a company making an expensive choice.

Since 2022, Meta has eliminated approximately 25,000 positions across multiple rounds of cuts. The May 2026 restructuring is the largest since the Year of Efficiency, but the framing is different. Zuckerberg is not correcting a hiring binge. He is redirecting resources toward AI at a scale that would have seemed implausible three years ago, and asking the people who remain to believe the destination is worth the cost of getting there.
